market_holds: Spot $4.63 at 18:08 UTC on the run day, which is a 52-week low (0.01% above it), -6.65% over 5 days, -21.65% over 20 days and -54.8% from the 52-week high (sealed baseline). The front Nov-20 straddle implies 8.53%. Puts are about 16 vol points cheaper than calls and put/call open interest is 0.17, so options holders are retail and lean bullish. Short interest is 41.6m shares (about 5-6% of float, 3.0 days to cover, settlement 2026-09-30). Consensus as seen in search snippets is Q3 revenue about $214-223M and EPS about $0.06. Chartmill lists $222.7M and says the revenue estimate was revised up about 17% over three months; another snippet says $214.3M. Both are undated and could not be opened (403). Either figure implies +8-12% q/q on Q2's $198.8M and +37-42% y/y. The company gave no numeric guide. On the Q2 call it said July options were steady, July equities softer than June, August tracking June, and H2 marketing 'similar in quantum to the first half' (H1 was $84.5M). The stock's fall since October is not about the business: the House China Select Committee report (Oct 7, -18% that day), class actions, a FINRA $4.2M fine (Nov 5), and a selling shareholder (CGH, from the Pi Securities deal) unloading up to 12.29M shares at up to 10% of daily volume until Dec 24. Webull can buy those shares back at VWAP. The last four prints traded on profit, not revenue. Q4'25 had a revenue beat and an EPS miss, and the stock fell. Q1'26 was a loss on 68% opex growth, -6.3%. Q2'26 posted record operating profit and was up 11-14% after hours and in premarket, but closed only +2.4%. Q3'25 was a beat and the stock still sold off.
view: This looks like an in-line quarter for a stock whose price is being set by things outside the quarter. Industry data for Jul-Sep is mixed. Robinhood's Q3 equity notional rose about 4% q/q and its options contracts about 17% q/q. Cboe's market-wide single-stock options ADV fell 8% q/q, but retail flow hit a record in September. Webull's own management said July and August ran at about June's post-PDT levels. My bottom-up rebuild is order-flow rebates up 6-12%, handling charges up modestly plus one month of Pi Securities, interest roughly stable, and prediction markets growing. That gives about $212-219M of revenue: in line with the $214M consensus and a little short of the $222.7M figure. Expenses probably rise. Marketing guided to about H1's quantum implies roughly $40M+ against Q2's $35M, and G&A carries legal and regulatory costs and the Pi consolidation. So EPS is near the $0.06 consensus with no clear beat. The reaction at the open will probably turn on two things the numbers do not settle. First, how management handles the China report and the CGH overhang; a buyback of the overhang shares at VWAP would be a real positive. Second, the expense line, which has decided three of the last four reactions. A beaten-down stock at an all-time low with bullish retail options could bounce on a clean print. A stock that fell after three of its last four prints, in a sector where Robinhood fell about 6% after hours on its own Q3 expenses, could just as easily fall. I see no unpriced direction.

recommendation.reason: Independent Q3 data from Robinhood, Cboe and Webull's own commentary on July and August rebuilds to revenue in line with consensus, not clearly above it. Guided marketing spend points to flat-to-down margin from Q2. The forces actually driving the stock (the China report, the CGH share overhang, litigation) will not be settled by the release's numbers. I see nothing the consensus misses, so no trade.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: An announcement on the release or call that Webull is buying the CGH overhang shares at VWAP or stepping up the $100M buyback, together with revenue well above $225M. That would make the bounce case likely at the open.

self_critique: The strongest case for a long: the stock is at an all-time low after a 22% fall driven by things outside the business, retail options lean bullish, and fundamentals run about +40% y/y. Q2 showed a clean profit beat can gap the stock 10%+ at the open, and a September record in retail flow plus prediction markets during football season could push revenue past $225M. Management could also neutralise the overhang by buying it back. The strongest case for a short: the higher consensus figure ($222.7M, revised up 17%) may be above what the data supports, marketing rises, and a stock under a China cloud may sell any rally to the mechanical seller. Each side is plausible, so I stay at about 50.
approach_notes: Rebuilding the line from counterparties' data (P3, own arithmetic) did the most work and showed the consensus is roughly right. P6 (find the line it trades on) pointed to profit and expenses. The thin, undated consensus pages limited how sharply I could test the bar.
